import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Age distribution
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
current_year = 2014  # Based on the dates in the dataset
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']
ax1.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel('Age')
ax1.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax1.set_title('Customer Age Distribution')
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Income distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
df['Income'].dropna().hist(bins=25, ax=ax2, color='coral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_xlabel('Income')
ax2.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax2.set_title('Income Distribution')
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Education level
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
education_counts = df['Education'].value_counts()
ax3.bar(range(len(education_counts)), education_counts.values, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black')
ax3.set_xticks(range(len(education_counts)))
ax3.set_xticklabels(education_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')
ax3.set_title('Education Level Distribution')
ax3.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 4. Spending patterns
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_means = df[spending_cols].mean()
colors_spend = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(spending_cols)))
bars = ax4.bar(range(len(spending_cols)), spending_means.values, color=colors_spend, edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_xticks(range(len(spending_cols)))
ax4.set_xticklabels(['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold'], rotation=45, ha='right')
ax4.set_ylabel('Average Spending')
ax4.set_title('Average Spending by Product Category')
ax4.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 5. Purchase channels
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
purchase_channels = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
channel_sums = df[purchase_channels].sum()
colors_pie = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff', '#99ff99']
ax5.pie(channel_sums.values, labels=['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store'], 
        autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors_pie, startangle=90)
ax5.set_title('Purchase Channel Distribution')

# 6. Marital Status
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax6.bar(range(len(marital_counts)), marital_counts.values, color='plum', edgecolor='black')
ax6.set_xticks(range(len(marital_counts)))
ax6.set_xticklabels(marital_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')
ax6.set_ylabel('Count')
ax6.set_title('Marital Status Distribution')
ax6.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 7. Income vs Total Spending
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
scatter = ax7.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], 
                     c=df['Age'], cmap='viridis', alpha=0.6, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax7.set_xlabel('Income')
ax7.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax7.set_title('Income vs Total Spending (colored by Age)')
plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax7, label='Age')
ax7.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 8. Campaign Response Rate
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
response_rates = df[campaign_cols].mean() * 100
ax8.barh(range(len(campaign_cols)), response_rates.values, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
ax8.set_yticks(range(len(campaign_cols)))
ax8.set_yticklabels(['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response'])
ax8.set_xlabel('Acceptance Rate (%)')
ax8.set_title('Campaign Response Rates')
ax8.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='x')

plt.suptitle('Customer Marketing Data Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
